subject: On‑prem connector certification, no‑train commitment & export timeline
messages:
From: Emma Thompson <emma.thompson@therahealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@therahealth.com>, legal@therahealth.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On‑prem connector and data use commitments

Neha,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — TheraHealth is excited about the on‑prem connector path for our clinical intake forms. A few items legal and security asked us to confirm before we proceed to PO: 

- We need a contractual "no‑training/no‑improvement" commitment (no model updates using our data, including derivatives), or a documented operational isolation that guarantees no training.
- Evidence of subprocessor isolation when using the connector (a simple cert and an inventory).
- Export timeline and process for a full patient‑facing transcript export (SFTP vs API), plus proof of deletion once the export completes.
- KMS integration options for customer‑controlled keys.

Can you outline the technical flow and provide an operational checklist we can share internally? Also include any artifacts we can attach to our procurement packet.

Best,
Emma Thompson
Head of Partnerships, TheraHealth

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Emma Thompson <emma.thompson@therahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem connector and data use commitments

Emma — thanks for the clear list. High level answers first, then I attach an operational checklist we've prepared for similar customers.

1) No‑train commitment: Redwood can commit contractually to "no training" on TheraHealth production inputs for the hosted model fleet. For an on‑prem connector, the default is customer data never leaves the customer's VPC — which operationally enforces no model improvement. We can add explicit language in the DPA and SOW stating "no model training, no derivative use" for customer data processed via the on‑prem connector.

2) Subprocessor isolation: I'll attach our current subprocessor map and a short cert of isolation for the on‑prem deployment path. For the hosted route we'd provide the usual subprocessor list; for on‑prem we document that no external inference subprocessors have access to tenant data.

3) Export timeline & proof of deletion: We support two export paths — SFTP (push) and API (pulled by customer). Typical timeline for a one‑time full export is 24–48 hours depending on data size; we can commit to a 72‑hour SLA for the first large export in the SOW. Deletion proof is a signed event log and an export manifest. We'll include a sample proof of deletion artifact in the checklist.

4) KMS: We support customer‑managed keys via KMS/HSM for private deployments. For hybrid connectors we provide guidance and a partner integration checklist.

I attached "No‑Train_Operational_Checklist.xlsx" (ops steps and artifacts) and "Redwood_Subprocessor_Map_202705.pdf".

Next steps: If this looks good to you, Marissa (sales/legal) will draft proposed contract language and Karthik will propose the SOW export SLA buckets. Jonas, can you confirm the operational tasks and a tentative rollout timeline?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Trust & Policy
Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem connector and data use commitments

Neha / team — quick ops confirmation and proposed timeline.

On‑prem connector technical flow (short):
- Customer deploys connector VM into their VPC; all inference requests and KV cache remain in VPC.
- Telemetry: optional minimal telemetry only for health; no business/text payload included unless customer opts in.
- Key material: customer KMS keys for any persisted artifacts; we provide an ISO audit hook.
- Export: export tool packages transcripts, writes manifest, and pushes to customer's SFTP or signs a URL for API pull.
- Deletion: connector runs a secure wipe job; generates a timestamped event signed by the customer's KMS identity.

Tentative timeline (assuming PO within 2 weeks):
- Week 0: SOW signed, kick‑off call, initial inventory of endpoints and KMS setup.
- Week 1: Connector build/config, security review with TheraHealth IAM team.
- Week 2: Staging run, end‑to‑end export test (SFTP).
- Week 3: Production cutover and handover.

Risks/notes: Larger transcript volumes (>200GB) push export to multi‑day window; we'll include a staging export rehearsal in the schedule.

Attachments referenced in the checklist include the sample deletion manifest format and the audit event fields.

— Jonas
Senior Engineering Manager, Deployments

From: Emma Thompson <emma.thompson@therahealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@therahealth.com>, legal@therahealth.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem connector and data use commitments

Neha / team — this is really helpful, thanks. A couple of follow ups from legal after reviewing your checklist: 

- Can you produce a one‑page "no‑train attestation" on Redwood letterhead that we can file? They want something signed stating there will be no model improvement or derivative training from processing done by the connector.
- For the deletion proof: can we get the manifest output in JSON schema (sample) and an example audit event showing the KMS signature? That will speed our security signoff.
- Procurement asked whether the 72‑hour initial export SLA is negotiable — they prefer 48 hours for go‑live; is that feasible for under 100GB?

If you can send the attestation and sample JSON manifest today, I can push procurement and legal to move.

Thanks,
Emma
